invariants.finding: D2 defines one reusable per-level exchange law for the common SWAP kernel, not a use-case-specific SWAP version.
The D2 component contract contains no file paths, parsing, file units or legacy I/O semantics.
Immutable exchange parameters, hydraulic inputs, scratch and results are separated explicitly.
The exchange law has no persistent physical state; DRAINL, DIFFL and WETPER are not migrated as column state.
Wet perimeter, temporary resistances and branch temporaries are worker/job scratch.
Immutable per-level parameters are shareable and compatible with SoA/batched layouts.
D2 returns trial transfers only; commit/rollback ownership remains runtime composition.
A stateless law is cheap to recompute from the same committed hydraulic state and changed control head.
No day/month/year unit or calendar boundary is embedded in the exchange evaluator.
The law is evaluated for whatever generic coupling/solver interval supplies its instantaneous hydraulic inputs.
Branch diagnostics and sensitivities are exposed so later coupling/runtime composition can use them transactionally.
D2 does not alter the direct SWAP-MODFLOW head/flux interface; it publishes a signed lateral physical transfer.
The returned signed exchange is authoritative physical mass transfer; no tolerance or tangent failure may erase finite mass.
Physical sensitivities with respect to groundwater level, control head and ponding are first-class outputs where defined.
Analytic branch sensitivities avoid mandatory perturbation reruns; perturbations remain qualification references only.
The law is stateless and parameter-shareable, suitable for large homogeneous MultiSWAP batches.
No MODFLOW-cell fractions or tile topology appear inside the exchange law.
Deep-vadose transfer remains external and unrelated to this lateral drainage exchange law.
D2 neither owns nor transforms storage between components; no cross-component water can disappear here.
The law depends on an explicit hydraulic summary/control head, not on one particular Richards implementation.
Existing qualified drainage/interflow response science is reused conceptually; legacy globals/module boundaries are not.
No HeadCalc arrays or internal solver variables are referenced; groundwater level enters through a clean hydraulic input.
Physical options such as open/tube drain and highest-level surface mode are separated from numerical solver policy.
Per-level evaluation has bounded constant cost; difficult branch points are diagnosed rather than iterated internally.
Frozen branch-exact behavior remains the reference target within the deliberately admitted domain; held seams are not silently altered.
Branch, suppression, cap, tangent-availability and source-seam diagnostics are required outputs.
No optional exchange option creates persistent state; inactive options cost no column state memory.
Runtime/coupler remains owner of aggregation, limiter ordering, storage evolution and external topology.
No midnight, daily execution, .dra parsing or direct MODFLOW assumption is introduced.
The D2 decomposition and all identified source seams are explicitly checked against all architecture invariants.

source_seam_holds: D2-RISK-01 SWSRF=1 undefined local WL remains excluded.
D2-RISK-02 negative extended power-interflow remains excluded.
D2-RISK-03 GWL=-0.1 pond-addition discontinuity must remain explicit.
D2-RISK-04 ZBOTDR+0.001 activation seam must remain explicit.
D2-RISK-05 GWLINF cap tangent kink must remain explicit.
D2-RISK-06 highest-level surface-drainage resistance kink must remain explicit.
D2-RISK-07 drainage/infiltration resistance zero-head branch point must remain explicit.
D2-RISK-08 PONDMX suppression seam must remain explicit.
scope_holds: No production source is admitted by F-PM08D2 readiness.
No storage-availability limiter is part of the constitutive law.
No multilevel aggregation or DIVDRA allocation is implemented here.
No SWST/WLSTAR ownership or surface-water balance is introduced.
No solver-side smoothing or hidden regularization is prequalified.
